findings.title: The SF2 repair overshot its named scope and renamed the DR-G15 artifact into the DR-103 lineage: nine sites now read 'g15 component-manifest leftover-join.v6', a name no artifact bears and which the subject's own pinned path contradicts
findings.finding: CLAUDE-CMLJ-V10-SF2 asked for a lineage prefix at exactly two sites and said so: 'Prefix the token in basedOn.occupancyV9.role … Sweep basedOn.d174.role to the same form. Change nothing else: … keep g15 leftover-join.v6 as the current G15 GATE leftover-join, keep every pin and digest, and do not touch the frozen predecessors.' Those two sites are correctly repaired. But the repair was then applied as a global sweep, and at nine further sites it fired on tokens that already carried the CORRECT prefix 'g15 ', producing 'g15 component-manifest leftover-join.v6'. That string names no artifact. The artifact meant is docs/coop/artifacts/g15-leftover-join.v6.json, which the subject itself pins at basedOn.g15JoinV6.path and whose own bytes self-name it 'g15-leftover-join.v6' with registerRow DR-G15. The nearest artifact the new string does name — 'component-manifest leftover-join.v6' — is docs/coop/artifacts/component-manifest-leftover-join.v6.json (9953f969…), a DR-103 join recorded at D-174, which is not the G15 GATE leftover-join and never was. The subject therefore asserts, nine times, a currency proposition about the wrong lineage: registerRowNote reads 'g15 component-manifest leftover-join.v6 remains the current G15 GATE leftover-join (D-290; registerRow DR-G15)', and basedOn.g15JoinV6.role reads 'g15 component-manifest leftover-join.v6 is that join.'
findings.whyThisMatters: The defect is self-refuting on the subject's own bytes, three ways at once. (1) Each of those same sentences also states 'g15 leftover-join and component-manifest leftover-join are different lineages; their version numbers are unrelated' — the sentence asserts the separation while the token collapses it. (2) The subject's own remeasurementClause still writes the correct name twice ('g15 leftover-join.v6, packaging leftover-join.v4' and 'Frozen g15 leftover-join.v6 remains current G15 GATE leftover-join'), so a single artifact now carries two different names for one pinned file and gives a reader no way to know which is the identifier. (3) obligations[2].reason contains both forms in adjacent clauses, with 'packaging leftover-join.v4' correctly prefixed one clause later, showing the sweep was mechanical rather than reasoned. This is a stronger defect than the bare-token class the lineage has twice REJECTED on (CMLJ-V7-SF1, CLAUDE-CMLJ-V10-SF2): a bare token is ambiguous, but 'g15 component-manifest leftover-join.v6' is affirmatively wrong, and the wrong referent it points at exists, is pinned in the same file, and carries a different register row. D-290's own adopted commit subject is 'D-290: record g15 leftover-join.v6'; the subject now cites D-290 under a name D-290 did not use.

findings.finding: landsNote contains two sentences that cannot both be true. Sentence 6: 'component-manifest leftover-join.v11 lands no new finding identifier and re-lands nothing.' Sentence 9: 'component-manifest leftover-join.v11 lands CLAUDE-CMLJ-V10-SF1 and CLAUDE-CMLJ-V10-SF2 and re-lands nothing else.' Sentence 6 is carried verbatim from v10, where it was true; sentence 9 is new. authorityClaim ('It lands CLAUDE-CMLJ-V10-SF1 and CLAUDE-CMLJ-V10-SF2') and purpose both take sentence 9's side, so sentence 6 is the false one — but the arrays take sentence 6's side. The lands array is byte-identical to v10's eleven members and carries neither CLAUDE-CMLJ-V10-SF1 nor CLAUDE-CMLJ-V10-SF2. findingDisposition is byte-identical to v10's eleven entries and carries no disposition for either identifier. The landsNote opener also still reads 'Cumulative landing record of this lineage, carried.' with no 'and extended', and its per-version enumeration stops at leftover-join.v9 and never says where CLAUDE-CMLJ-V10-SF1 and CLAUDE-CMLJ-V10-SF2 landed.
findings.whyThisMatters: This lineage has an explicit, twice-executed convention for what a landing version looks like, and this artifact matches the non-landing shape while claiming the landing one. v8 landed three predecessor findings: its landsNote reads 'carried from leftover-join.v6 and extended by this v8 … This v8 lands CMLJ-V7-SF1, CLAUDE-CMLJ-V7-SF1, CLAUDE-CMLJ-V7-SF2', and its lands array grew from 5 to 8 members while findingDisposition grew from 5 to 8 entries. v9 landed three more: 'carried and extended … This v9 lands CMLJ-V8-SF1, CMLJ-V8-SF2, CLAUDE-CMLJ-V8-SF1', lands 8 to 11, findingDisposition 8 to 11. v10 landed nothing: 'carried.' and 'lands no new finding identifier', arrays unchanged at 11. So in this lineage the sentence 'lands no new finding identifier' means precisely 'the lands array is not extended', and v11 asserts it while also asserting the opposite. The consequence is not cosmetic: this successor exists to land two findings, and after it is recorded there is no machine-checkable record anywhere in the artifact that CLAUDE-CMLJ-V10-SF1 or CLAUDE-CMLJ-V10-SF2 was ever dispositioned. A later MF-6 or successor auditor walking lands and findingDisposition against the lineage reads v11 as a version that landed nothing, which is the shape v10 legitimately had. The lineage already REJECTED v8 in part for a lands-record inconsistency of exactly this family — the subject's own basedOn.predecessorV8.role records it: v8 'stated in purpose that the lands record was carried while leftover-join.v8 also extended it.' v11 reproduces that defect with the arrays on the wrong side of the claim.
